summary: Dedicated (H100): higher p99 latency after runtime upgrade to 1.22 (profile pack enablement)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports elevated tail latency (p99) on Dedicated H100 after upgrading runtime to 1.22.x.
- p50/p95 largely unchanged; regression is concentrated at p99 during mixed prompt length traffic.

Impact
- Customer observed ~18–30% increase in p99 end-to-end latency for chat completions.
- No increase in 5xx rate reported; some client-side timeouts triggered due to tighter upstream timeout budget.

Environment
- Deployment mode: Dedicated
- Hardware: H100
- Region: us-east
- Runtime versions:
  - Before: runtime 1.21.4 (customer baseline)
  - After: runtime 1.22.0
- Profiles:
  - After upgrade, profile pack was enabled by default; active profile_id reported as h100/default (profile_version 1.0.0)

Workload details (from customer)
- Endpoint: /v1/chat.completions (streaming)
- Typical prompt length: mixed (short prompts + occasional long context)
- Typical output length: 150–500 tokens
- Concurrency: bursty; customer estimates 40–80 concurrent requests during peak

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Run traffic replay against Dedicated endpoint on runtime 1.21.4 (capture p50/p95/p99).
2) Upgrade to runtime 1.22.0.
3) Re-run same traffic replay; p99 increases notably.

Customer-provided evidence
- Example request IDs (anonymized) with timestamps provided in Zendesk handoff.
- Customer notes p99 correlates with periods of mixed prompt lengths (long prefill requests present).

Initial hypothesis
- Scheduler/batching defaults changed with profile pack enablement on H100. Possible over-aggressive batching under mixed prefill/decode leading to queueing spikes (tail latency).

Support request
- Confirm whether runtime 1.22 changed default scheduler/batching behavior on H100.
- Provide mitigation (pinning profile_version or adjusting overrides) and ETA for fix if regression confirmed.
comments:
[2026-02-06 09:12] Sean Gallagher (Reporter)
Created from escalation via CS. Customer upgraded Dedicated H100 to runtime 1.22.0 yesterday; seeing p99 regression. Looping in SRE + runtime owners.

[2026-02-06 09:26] Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Thanks. Can you share: (1) exact runtime build SHA from /health, (2) active profile_id/profile_version from debug bundle, (3) a 30–60 min window of request volume + latency chart? If customer can provide 10–20 request IDs around a p99 spike, that helps.

[2026-02-06 10:03] Sean Gallagher
Added artifacts to internal folder (not customer-visible):
- /health shows runtime 1.22.0, git_sha 6d3a9e1
- debug: profile_pack_enabled=true, active_profile_id=h100/default, profile_version=1.0.0
- p99 regression starts immediately after upgrade; p50/p95 stable.
- No elevated 5xx; client timeouts increased due to p99.

[2026-02-06 10:41] Allison Grant
Checked Runtime Profiles dashboard (internal): for this tenant’s pool, scheduler_queue_ms p99 shows spikes coincident with mixed workload periods. Kernel fallback counters look normal (no abnormal fallback rate). This looks like queueing/batching, not kernel selection.

[2026-02-06 11:10] Rafael Mendes
Correlates with ongoing canary investigation thread (#incidents / tail latency after profile tweak). Suspect H100 profile batching default introduced in 1.22.0 is too aggressive for mixed prefill/decode.
Mitigation options (Dedicated):
1) Pin profile_version back to last known-good (disable new defaults) OR
2) Apply override to reduce max_batch_tokens / cap concurrency.
Requesting runtime team guidance on safest knob set.

[2026-02-06 11:28] Sofia Ivanova
Agree with hypothesis. We saw a similar pattern in Hosted canary: queueing spikes under mixed prompt lengths when batching target is too high. We have a proposed fix to revert one batching default and tighten queue limits.
Recommended immediate mitigation for Dedicated: pin to profile_version=0.9.7 (pre-1.22 defaults) while we roll 1.0.1.

[2026-02-06 12:02] Rafael Mendes
Action: Provided customer with mitigation: pin profile_version=0.9.7 (or disable profile pack via Dedicated config flag) and redeploy. Also suggested temporarily reducing concurrency cap by ~15% during peak as an additional safety net.

[2026-02-07 08:19] Sean Gallagher
Customer confirmed pinning profile_version reduced p99 back near baseline within 30 minutes. They can operate on pinned version until fix lands.

[2026-02-07 10:37] Rafael Mendes
Tracking fix landing via PR https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/24988 (revert overly aggressive batching default causing p99 regression). Once merged and rolled to 1.22.1 / profile_version 1.0.1, we can advise unpin.

[2026-02-09 15:05] Connor O'Brien
Release note: hotfix will be included in runtime 1.22.1 and profile pack 1.0.1. Dedicated customers remain opt-in to default changes; pins are supported.

[2026-02-10 09:22] Rafael Mendes
Customer notified: runtime 1.22.1 available; recommended upgrade path:
1) upgrade to runtime 1.22.1
2) keep pin in place for 24h
3) remove pin to adopt profile_version 1.0.1 during off-peak (with rollback plan)
Also included instructions to verify active profile_version via /health and startup log summary.

[2026-02-10 11:10] Sean Gallagher
Customer acknowledged plan; will test off-peak. Closing as Resolved with mitigation and fix available.

Resolution
- Immediate workaround: customer pinned profile_version to pre-regression version to restore baseline p99.
- Permanent fix: batching default adjusted in runtime 1.22.1 / profile pack 1.0.1; customer can unpin after validating.

Follow-ups
- Ensure dedicated runbook includes: how to pin profile_version + verify in debug bundle.
- Confirm perf-canary gate covers mixed prompt-length workload for H100 to prevent recurrence.
